text: That embarrassing thing you did today?
And there's a study to prove it.
At Cornell University, psychologists made students wear a T-shirt with a giant picture of Barry Manilow on the front.
For a college student, this was about as uncool as it gets.
Then they sent them into a room full of other students.
Afterwards, they asked: how many people do you think noticed your shirt?
The students guessed half the room.
A giant, embarrassing face on their chest, and most people didn't even see it.
Psychologists call this the spotlight effect.
You feel like everyone's watching you.
But everyone else is too busy worrying about themselves.
